placement.frame: x forward (the way the toes point and the camera looks), y left, z up. The left leg is the one built from the mirrored yoke, on the torso cradle at y = +57.
placement.servo_in_cradle: Case bottom on the plate, long sides between the rails, centred along the rails, output shaft away from the plate.
placement.roll_servo_flip: true puts the hip roll shaft at the upper end of the torso cradle.
placement.pitch_servo_flip: true puts the hip pitch shaft at the lower end of the yoke cradle.
placement.knee_servo_flip: false puts the knee shaft at the far (distal) end of the thigh.
placement.horn_side: The printed blank sits on the outer face of the horn, so the horn screw is reached through the 8 mm hole from the far side.
placement.yoke_face: The roll horn meets the yoke face at yoke z = 0; the wall and the pitch cradle extend forward from it.
placement.thigh_face: 'rail' puts the hip horn on the face that carries the rails, so the knee servo lies beside the hip pitch servo and the foot is nearer the body. 'flat' puts it on the flat face, stacking thigh, knee servo and shin outward. Both are checked; this value picks the one the robot description uses.
placement.shin_face: The shin blank is symmetric; the face towards the knee servo meets the horn and the foot points +x.
placement.neutral: Thighs straight down, shins vertical, soles level, horns at mid travel.
placement.camera: The camera board stands in the mount at the front edge of the deck, lower edge on the corner seats, back face on the ledges, lens towards +x. The numbers repeat CAMERA, CAM_BACK_X, CAM_BASE_Z and CAM_TILT of build.py in the design directory; a test compares them with the parameters.json the generator writes.
placement.feet: 'comb' soles have fingers that cross the centre line between the fingers of the other sole; 'flat' is the plate as first drawn. FEET in build.py chooses the same. Joint limits are taken from sweeps that leave contact between the two shin parts out, because whether the soles meet depends on both legs together; the feet section of the report says how far the legs may move against each other.
placement.face: The default head is the round display as the eyes with the camera board above it ('eyes_above'); 'eyes_below' puts the camera under the display. FACE and CAMERA in build.py choose the same. Where the display, the camera board and the battery are is read from the parameters.json the generator writes. Without a face the camera stands alone in the fixed mount, placed by the numbers under 'camera'.
placement.front: Forward is the way the toes point: each foot plate reaches 46.5 mm ahead of the shin and 28.5 mm behind it (build.py moves it 9 mm towards +x), and the design README says toes forward. The hip roll cradles open towards +x, so the hips and legs stand ahead of the deck by construction.
placement.board: UNO Q long side along x, centred between the deck rails, on spacers; Braccio shield stacked on top.

findings.text: Each cradle has 4 tie slot pairs; on every cradle at least 2 of the tie paths cross the case clear of the output shaft and horn (the pairs at the shaft end do not, and are for a servo lying the other way round). This depends on the assumed shaft position and horn size.
Every servo case fits between its rails with 0.5 mm each side, sits fully on its plate, and all tie slots are open.
All six horn screw holes are on their shaft axes and a screwdriver has a free path to each at the neutral pose.

The AI-Thinker ESP32-CAM stands in its mount with 0.5 mm each side and 0.3 mm of play under the snap lips, on the corner seats, overlapping the print by 0.0 mm3. The mount is 5.06 mm from the UNO Q and 5.34 mm from the space kept for the shield and its plugs.

The lens looks along +x, the way the toes point, 10.0 degrees below level, 266.95 mm above the floor at the stand pose. A cone of 40.0 degrees half angle in front of it is clear at the neutral and stand poses. A leg comes into the cone with left_hip_pitch between -90.0 and -21.0 degrees; right_hip_pitch between -90.0 and -24.0 degrees (one joint moved, the others at the stand or neutral pose).

23 pin holes and 32 studs compatible with LEGO Technic and System elements: every hole is open for a 4.8 mm pin over 7.8 mm with wall all round, none is nearer than 14.78 mm to a joint axis or 2.71 mm to another part at the neutral pose, and none is in the camera's clear cone. Whether a real pin or brick holds in a printed one is not known.
Legs straight down: the centre of mass is 2.74 mm outside the support polygon of the two feet (behind the heels); it falls backward.
With the thighs swung back 52.0 degrees and the knees turned the other way to keep the soles level, the centre of mass is 46.8 mm inside the polygon. This is the stand pose.

On one foot the centre of mass is inside the sole at the stand pose: 32.07 mm on the left foot alone and 21.26 mm on the right, with the other foot level with it. The soles reach across the centre line, so no weight shift is needed. This is static and rigid: the fingers, the shin plate and the servos give under the load.
